The NEHA MITTAL MITTAL Date:
2024.10.03 16:14:54 +0530 documents relied upon by the plaintiff to prove his title are GPA, Agreement to Sell, Will, Affidavit, Receipt, Possession Letter Ex.PW-1/3 (Colly).
Admittedly, no ownership can be created in immovable property on the basis of aforesaid documents.
So, the first question before this court is whether the plaintiff can seek recovery of possession of the suit property on the basis of documents Ex.PW-1/3 (Colly).

It has been held by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in judgment Karamvir Singh Vs. Man Singh MANU/DE/2364/2014 as under :-
"The appellants/plaintiffs therefore may not in the strict sense be owners of the property, but, in a suit for possession or for injunction, a plaintiff has only to prove an entitlement to the suit property which is better than the respondent/defendant.

entities.text: Karamvir Singh Vs. Man Singh MANU/DE/2364/2014
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Once the appellant/ plaintiffs prove an entitlement better than the respondents/
defendants, it is upon the respondents/ defendants to discharge the onus that they have a better entitlement to the suit property than as is pleaded by the appellants/
plaintiffs.

In this case, the respondents/ defendants have not shown any vestige of title for they being entitled to the possession of the suit property, and the appellants/plaintiffs have duly shown their entitlement by virtue of registered power of attorney dated 10.08.2009.

Accordingly, I hold that the appellants/ plaintiffs had a better title than the respondents/defendants and were therefore entitled to the relief that the respondents/defendants should be injunctive from illegally dispossessing the appellants/plaintiffs from the suit property."

16. In 'Ramesh Chand vs Suresh Chand' decided on 09.04.2012 by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, it was held as under :
"12 ..... A right to possession of an immovable property arises not only from a complete ownership right in the property but having a better title or a better entitlement/ NEHA MITTAL MITTAL Date:
2024.10.03 16:15:03 +0530 right to the possession of the property than qua the person who is in actual physical possession thereof....."

17. The defendants have asserted their right in the suit property on the basis of bayana receipt Ex.DW-1/1 by averring that the defendant no.1 is the owner of the suit property though the title documents were executed in favour of the plaintiff in lieu of the financial help extended by him.
Admittedly, no right in the suit property can be created in favour of the defendants on the basis of said bayana receipt.

Further, it is also possible that the erstwhile owner Leela Ram might have Sanjay Gupta vs Arjun Sahani Anr on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38781115/

sentences.text: The defendants admit the fact that documents Ex.PW-1/3(Colly) have been executed in favour of the plaintiff.
Accordingly, the defence raised by the defendant is inadmissible in view of Section 91 and 92 of Indian Evidence Act which deals with the exclusivity of documented evidence.
Oral evidence is only permitted as an exception to prove the agreement and the applicable exceptions are outlined in Section 92.
Further, DW-3 has also admitted that her husband Leela Ram had executed documents Ex.PW-1/3 (Colly) in favour of the plaintiff.

Though, the defendants and DW-3 have consistently deposed that documents PW-1/3(Colly) were executed in favour of the plaintiff as defendant no.1 was not having the entire sale consideration with him but the same will not have any impact on the fate of the case as admittedly, no document has been executed in favour of defendant no.1.
18.

However, the defendants have failed to explain as to why the alleged correct market value of the suit property was not mentioned in the said documents as the same were executed in favour of the plaintiff with their consent.
Further, no evidence has been led by the defendants to show that they have made payment of part of consideration amount, as claimed by them.
19. In view of the above discussion, this court is of the opinion that the plaintiff has discharged the burden of proof placed upon him.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants.

It appears that the damages has been inadvertently quantified as Rs.12,000/- at the time of framing of issue as in the prayer clause, the plaintiff has sought damages/mesne profits @
Rs.6,000/- p.m. for the illegal use of the suit property from 25.08.2015 till the date of actual physical possession is handed over to the plaintiff.
25. The plaintiff has submitted that mesne profits for unauthorized occupation of the suit property by the defendants shall be payable from 25.08.2015.
The legal notice Ex. PW-1/6 has been served upon the defendants as per acknowledgment card Ex.PW-1/7 and thus, the tenancy of the defendants stands terminated from the service of legal notice.
Hence, the defendant would be said to be in unauthorized possession over the suit property since thereafter and thus, plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits from 28.05.2015 as prayed.
Now, it is to be examined as to at what rate, mesne profits shall be awarded to the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has claimed mesne profits at the rate of Rs.6,000 per month.
He should have produced the evidence to prove that Rs.6,000 per month would have been reasonable compensation for his deprivation of possession of the suit property from the defendant.
However, in the absence of any evidence, the Court can take judicial notice that there had been steep rise in the rent of the properties in Delhi.

The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in NEHA MITTAL MITTAL Date:
2024.10.03 16:15:43 +0530 Vinod Khanna v. Bakshi Sachdev (Deceased) through LRs, AIR 1996 Delhi 32, has held that:
21.
[I]t is true that no substantial evidence has been led by the plaintiffs in respect of the increase of rent in the properties like that of the suit property.

However, it is a well known fact that the amount of rent for various properties in and around Delhi has been rising staggeringly and we cannot see why such judicial notice could not be taken of the fact about such increase of rents in the premises in and around Delhi which is a city of growing importance being the capital of the country which is a matter of public history.
At this stage we may appropriately refer to the Court taking judicial notice of the increase of price of land rapidly in the urban areas in connection with the land acquisition matters.

Even the Apex Court has taken judicial notice of the fact of universal escalation of rent and even raised rent of disputed premises by taking such judicial notice in case of D.C. Oswal v. V.K. Subbiah, AIR 1992 SC 184 :
1992(1) RCR 326(SC).

22. In that view of the matter we have no hesitation in our mind in holding that the trial court did not commit any illegality in taking judicial notice of the fact of increase of rents and determining the compensation in respect of the suit premises at Rs.10,000/- per month w.e.f. 19.1.1989, in view of the fact that the rent fixed for the said premises was at Rs. 6,000/- per month as far back as in the year 1974.
26.

Hence, considering the above said legal position in the present case, the Court is of the view that the plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits at rate of Rs.5,000 per month from 28.08.2015 till the handing over of the tenanted premises by the defendant to plaintiff.

Rs.6,000/- p.m. for the illegal use of the suit property from 25.08.2015 till the date of actual physical possession is handed over to the plaintiff.
The legal notice Ex. PW-1/6 has been served upon the defendants as per acknowledgment card Ex.PW-1/7 and thus, the tenancy of the defendants stands terminated from the service of legal notice.
Hence, the defendant would be said to be in unauthorized possession over the suit property since thereafter and thus, plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits from 28.05.2015 as prayed.
The plaintiff has claimed mesne profits at the rate of Rs.6,000 per month.
He should have produced the evidence to prove that Rs.6,000 per month would have been reasonable compensation for his deprivation of possession of the suit property from the defendant.
However, in the absence of any evidence, the Court can take judicial notice that there had been steep rise in the rent of the properties in Delhi.
The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in NEHA MITTAL MITTAL Date:
2024.10.03 16:15:43 +0530 Vinod Khanna v. Bakshi Sachdev (Deceased) through LRs, AIR 1996 Delhi 32, has held that:
21.
Even the Apex Court has taken judicial notice of the fact of universal escalation of rent and even raised rent of disputed premises by taking such judicial notice in case of D.C. Oswal v. V.K. Subbiah, AIR 1992 SC 184 :
1992(1) RCR 326(SC).
22. In that view of the matter we have no hesitation in our mind in holding that the trial court did not commit any illegality in taking judicial notice of the fact of increase of rents and determining the compensation in respect of the suit premises at Rs.10,000/- per month w.e.f. 19.1.1989, in view of the fact that the rent fixed for the said premises was at Rs. 6,000/- per month as far back as in the year 1974.
26.
Hence, considering the above said legal position in the present case, the Court is of the view that the plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits at rate of Rs.5,000 per month from 28.08.2015 till the handing over of the tenanted premises by the defendant to plaintiff.
